La palabra <em>álgebra</em> viene del tí: The word algebra comes from the title of al-Khwarizmi's book (Baghdad, around 820): al-jabr wa-l-muqabala, meaning “restoration and balancing”, that is, moving terms from one side of an equality to the other. For centuries everything was written out in words. Letters for the unknowns were introduced by François Viète at the end of the sixteenth century, and Descartes settled the convention we still follow: the last letters of the alphabet ($x, y, z$) for what is unknown and the first ones ($a, b, c$) for what is known.
